title: Unmarked cone straightening along a change of target is enriched left Kan extension
statement:
Use simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the small simplicial categories, coherent realization $\mathfrak C$, ordered cone $X\star\Delta^0$ with last vertex $v$, cone pushout and enriched natural transformations of [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen]. Fix a small simplicial set $S$, small simplicial categories $D$ and $D'$, a simplicial functor $\phi:\mathfrak C[S]\to D^{\mathrm{op}}$ and a simplicial functor $\pi:D\to D'$, and put $\phi'=\pi^{\mathrm{op}}\circ\phi:\mathfrak C[S]\to D'^{\mathrm{op}}$. For $a:X\to S$ and $\psi\in\{\phi,\phi'\}$ with target $E^{\mathrm{op}}$ ($E=D$ or $E=D'$), put $M_{a,\psi}=\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0]\amalg_{\mathfrak C[X]}E^{\mathrm{op}}$, the categorical pushout of simplicial categories along $\psi\circ\mathfrak C[a]$, and let $L_\psi(X):E\to\mathsf{sSet}$ be $e\mapsto M_{a,\psi}(e,v)$ with action by precomposition. Write $\pi^*G=G\circ\pi$ for a simplicial functor $G:D'\to\mathsf{sSet}$, and $\pi_!$ for enriched left Kan extension, the left adjoint of $\pi^*$ on simplicial functors and enriched natural transformations, characterized by natural bijections $\operatorname{Nat}(\pi_!H,G)\cong\operatorname{Nat}(H,\pi^*G)$.

The simplicial functor $M_{a,\phi}\to M_{a,\phi'}$ which is $\pi^{\mathrm{op}}$ on $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the identity on $\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0]$ fixes $v$ and induces a natural map $L_\phi(X)\to\pi^*L_{\phi'}(X)$. Its adjoint
$$\pi_!L_\phi(X)\longrightarrow L_{\phi'}(X)$$
is an isomorphism of simplicial functors $D'\to\mathsf{sSet}$, natural in $X$ over $S$. Equivalently, defining $U_\psi(G)$ to have as $n$-simplices over $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$ the enriched natural maps $L_\psi(\Delta^n\xrightarrow{\sigma}S)\to G$, with operators induced by simplex operators, there is an isomorphism of simplicial sets over $S$, $U_{\phi'}(G)\cong U_\phi(\pi^*G)$, natural in $G:D'\to\mathsf{sSet}$. These isomorphisms are the identity for $\pi=\mathrm{id}$, compatible with composites $D\to D'\to D''$, and compatible with maps $X\to Y$ over $S$. No Kan, local Kan, Dwyer--Kan, fibrancy or cofibrancy hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Section 2.2.1, the straightening construction (St_phi X)(C)=Map_M(C,v) (printed p.73), and Proposition 2.2.1.1(2) (printed p.74), which HTT calls an obvious functoriality property and states without proof; the right-adjoint form follows by adjunction. Read in the sandbox copy of the PDF (April 9, 2017 text); not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this result. The marked analogue is part of lem-coef-marked-cone-straightening-quillen, which assumes a locally Kan target and so does not apply to the identity of C[S].

proof.text: Put $A=\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0]$, $B=\mathfrak C[X]$, $M=M_{a,\phi}$ and $M'=M_{a,\phi'}$. Apply [lem-coef-cone-boundary-projective-cells] with target category $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ and attaching functor $\phi$, and then with target $D'{}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and attaching functor $\phi'$. Its structural clause says that the old full subcategories of $M,M'$ are exactly these targets, there are no mapping simplices from $v$ to an old object, and the endomorphism simplicial set of $v$ is $\Delta^0$. Their remaining mapping sets and precomposition actions are precisely $L_\phi(X)$ and $L_{\phi'}(X)$ by [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen]. The pushout gives $q:M\to M'$ which is $\pi^{\mathrm{op}}$ on the old part and the identity on $A$. Thus $q$ gives the stated enriched natural map $u:L_\phi(X)\to\pi^*L_{\phi'}(X)$.

source.place: Section 2.2.1, correspondence description of M (printed p.73); Proposition 2.2.1.1(2).

proof.text: Fix any simplicial functor $G:D'\to\mathsf{sSet}$. Form a simplicial category $E_G$ on the objects of $D'{}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and one new object $w$: its old mapping sets are unchanged, $E_G(e,w)=G(e)$, $E_G(w,e)=\varnothing$, and $E_G(w,w)=\Delta^0$. Composition into $w$ is the $G$-action; its associativity and unit equations are exactly the functor axioms of $G$. By Step 1, a functor $F':M'\to E_G$ which is the identity on the old part and sends $v$ to $w$ consists precisely of simplicial maps $L_{\phi'}(X)(e)\to G(e)$ commuting with the action. Such functors are therefore exactly enriched natural transformations $L_{\phi'}(X)\to G$. Likewise functors $F:M\to E_G$ whose old restriction is $\pi^{\mathrm{op}}$ and which send $v$ to $w$ correspond exactly to enriched natural transformations $L_\phi(X)\to\pi^*G$. There are no further composition equations: all nonidentity mixed composites end at $w$.

source.place: Section 2.2.1, correspondence description; explicit construction of a correspondence with prescribed outgoing mapping sets.

proof.text: Precomposition by $q$ gives a bijection between these two sets of functors. Here is its inverse. Given $F:M\to E_G$, restrict it to $A$ and pair this restriction with the inclusion $D'{}^{\mathrm{op}}\to E_G$. The two functors agree on $B$: on that subcategory $F$ is $\pi^{\mathrm{op}}\phi\mathfrak C[a]=\phi'\mathfrak C[a]$. The defining pushout of $M'$ therefore supplies a unique $F':M'\to E_G$. It fixes the old part and takes $v$ to $w$. The equality $F' q=F$ holds on both factors of the pushout defining $M$, hence everywhere. Conversely reconstructing from $F' q$ recovers $F'$, since both its $A$-restriction and its old restriction agree. Under Step 2 this is the bijection $\beta_G:\operatorname{Nat}(L_{\phi'}(X),G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Nat}(L_\phi(X),\pi^*G)$, $b\mapsto(\pi^*b)u$. Postcomposing by a transformation $G\to G'$ commutes with this formula, so the bijection is natural in $G$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.1.1(2): expansion using the two categorical pushout universal properties.

proof.text: Set $H=L_\phi(X)$, $K=L_{\phi'}(X)$ and $P=\pi_!H$, and let $\eta:H\to\pi^*P$ be the Kan-adjunction unit. The map in the statement is its adjunct $h:P\to K$ characterized by $(\pi^*h)\eta=u$. Define $t:K\to P$ to be the unique transformation with $\beta_P(t)=\eta$. Then $(\pi^*(th))\eta=(\pi^*t)u=\eta$, so injectivity of the Kan-adjunction bijection gives $th=1_P$. Also $\beta_K(ht)=(\pi^*h)\beta_P(t)=(\pi^*h)\eta=u=\beta_K(1_K)$, so injectivity of $\beta_K$ gives $ht=1_K$. Thus the specified adjunct $h$ is an isomorphism. This uses only the defining bijection for $\pi_!$ in the statement and Step 3; it requires neither a pointwise Kan-extension formula nor an enriched Yoneda theorem.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.1.1(2): explicit inverse from the two natural bijections.

proof.text: For a map $f:X\to Y$ over $S$, the induced cone maps and identity target maps give maps $M_X\to M_Y$ and $M'_X\to M'_Y$. Their square with $q_X,q_Y$ commutes because its two composites agree on $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ and on $\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0]$. Consequently $u_Y L_\phi(f)=(\pi^*L_{\phi'}(f))u_X$. Taking adjuncts gives $h_Y\pi_!L_\phi(f)=L_{\phi'}(f)h_X$, proving naturality of the specified isomorphism in $X$.

source.place: Section 2.2.1, cone-pushout functoriality in the input; Proposition 2.2.1.1(2).

proof.text: For each $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$, Step 3 gives a bijection $\beta_{G,\sigma}:\operatorname{Nat}(L_{\phi'}(\Delta^n\xrightarrow{\sigma}S),G)\to\operatorname{Nat}(L_\phi(\Delta^n\xrightarrow{\sigma}S),\pi^*G)$. If $\theta:[m]\to[n]$ is monotone, Step 5 says $u_\sigma L_\phi(\theta)=(\pi^*L_{\phi'}(\theta))u_{\sigma\theta}$; substituting this into the formula for $\beta$ shows that its bijections commute with restriction along $\theta$. The stated simplex definition of $U$ in [lem-coef-unmarked-straightening-quillen] therefore assembles them to the isomorphism $U_{\phi'}(G)\cong U_\phi(\pi^*G)$ over $S$. Naturality in $G$ is Step 3.

source.place: Section 2.2.1, direct right-adjoint construction; right-adjoint form of Proposition 2.2.1.1(2).

proof.text: For an identity target functor, the pushout map $q$ is the identity, so $u$ and $\beta$ are identities; the Kan-extension map is the identity under the canonical identification $\operatorname{id}_!H\cong H$ supplied by its defining adjunction. For $D\xrightarrow{\pi}D'\xrightarrow{\rho}D''$, the direct pushout map equals the composite of the two maps, since they agree on the cone factor and on $D^{\mathrm{op}}$. Hence $u_{\rho\pi}=(\pi^*u_\rho)u_\pi$, with the input $\phi'$ understood for $u_\rho$. The formula for $\beta$ now gives $\beta_{\rho\pi}=\beta_\pi\beta_\rho$ on every transformation. The composite $h_\rho\rho_!(h_\pi)$ has adjunct $u_{\rho\pi}$, so uniqueness of adjuncts identifies it with $h_{\rho\pi}$ under $(\rho\pi)_!\cong\rho_!\pi_!$. These are the canonical identifications from the composed adjunction bijections. Step 6 gives the same composite law for $U$ degreewise. All categories and mapping sets are small in the stated universes; no argument has used Kan or model-category hypotheses.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.1.1(2): identity and composite target substitutions, checked on the two pushout factors.

lean.statement: theorem unmarked_straightening_target_change (S : SSet.{u}) : ∃ (P : TargetChangePresentation S) (T : ∀ (D E : SCat.{u}) (π : D ⟶ E) (φ : rigidification.obj S ⟶ oppositeCategory D), TargetChangeComparison P π φ), (∀ (D : SCat.{u}) (φ : rigidification.obj S ⟶ oppositeCategory D) (X : Over S) (d : D), HEq (((T D D (𝟙 D) φ).unitMap.app X).app d) (𝟙 (((P.L D φ).obj X).functor.obj d))) ∧ (∀ (D E F : SCat.{u}) (π : D ⟶ E) (ρ : E ⟶ F) (φ : rigidification.obj S ⟶ oppositeCategory D) (X : Over S) (d : D), HEq (((T D F (π ≫ ρ) φ).unitMap.app X).app d) ((((T D E π φ).unitMap.app X).app d) ≫ (((T E F ρ (φ ≫ targetOpposite π)).unitMap.app X).app (π.obj d)))) ∧ (∀ (D : SCat.{u}) (φ : rigidification.obj S ⟶ oppositeCategory D) (G : Diagram D), HEq ((T D D (𝟙 D) φ).unstraightening.hom.app G).left (𝟙 (((P.U D φ).obj G).left))) ∧ (∀ (D E F : SCat.{u}) (π : D ⟶ E) (ρ : E ⟶ F) (φ : rigidification.obj S ⟶ oppositeCategory D) (G : Diagram F), HEq ((T D F (π ≫ ρ) φ).unstraightening.hom.app G).left (((T E F ρ (φ ≫ targetOpposite π)).unstraightening.hom.app G).left ≫ ((T D E π φ).unstraightening.hom.app ((targetRestriction ρ).obj G)).left))
lean.note: Canonical target restriction and the target-change pushout map have explicit data.
